cases.title: Three-phase N-diphenylmethyl hydrogenolysis
cases.protocol: N-Diphenylmethylazetidin-3-ol (DMAOL; MW 239.32 g/mol) was prepared as a 3.8 wt% solution in methanol. For molarity conversion, explicitly use and label an assumed solution density of 0.792 g/mL, giving approximately 0.126 M DMAOL. A 200 mL charge was contacted with hydrogen over 0.5 g of 7 wt% Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 catalyst in a stirred batch reactor at 60 °C and 21 bar for 5 h. Conversion to 3-azetidinol was 38.1%. Translate this into one conservative continuous-flow packed-bed screening design. Acetic acid is optional and must not be introduced unless explicitly justified as a screening variable. Report feed preparation, gas-liquid mixing, packed-bed operation, temperature, pressure basis, liquid flow, hydrogen inlet/STP flow, pressure-corrected in-channel hydrogen flow, hydrogen equivalents, nominal empty-bed space time, liquid-holdup/contact residence-time basis, separation, collection, startup, shutdown, nitrogen purge, and hydrogen/methanol/pressure safety controls.

cases.title: Two-step metal-free oxidative amidation
cases.protocol: Benzyl alcohol was oxidized to benzaldehyde in dioxane using aqueous H2O2 (2.0 equiv), NaBr (2 mol%), and H2SO4 (1 mol%) at 70 °C. After complete alcohol oxidation, morpholine and aqueous TBHP were added and the mixture was heated at 80 °C to form benzoyl morpholine. Conditions analogous to 0.667 M benzyl alcohol and 0.667 M morpholine/TBHP feeds were used. Performing the two oxidation stages sequentially in batch required 30 h and afforded benzoyl morpholine in 76% yield. Translate this procedure into one conservative, executable two-stage continuous-flow screening design. Explicitly report all three feed preparations, individual pump rates, first and second mixer assignments, stage temperatures, stage volumes, stage residence times, total process residence time, peroxide compatibility, startup order, steady-state collection, shutdown, aqueous work-up, and peroxide/acid/pressure safety controls.

cases.title: Highly exothermic dinitration of an N-alkyl aniline
cases.protocol: In the conventional industrial batch preparation of pendimethalin, a 30 wt% solution of N-(1-ethylpropyl)-3,4-xylidine in a chlorinated solvent is first treated with dilute nitric acid. The organic and spent-acid phases are separated, and the organic phase is then treated with more concentrated nitric acid. The two nitration stages require 4 h in total and afford an 89% combined yield of pendimethalin and N-nitroso-pendimethalin in a 7:3 ratio. The chemistry is a highly exothermic liquid-liquid nitration with possible decomposition and explosion hazards for nitro compounds. Translate this batch procedure into one conservative, executable continuous-flow screening design for pendimethalin. Report feed preparations, individual pump rates, nitric-acid equivalents, mixing and reactor assignments, temperature, reactor volume, residence time, collection, phase separation or quench, startup and shutdown, and thermal/corrosion safety controls.
